event.summary: The new live line fixtures still expose repaints to transfer admission
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: Considered whether replacing the old buffer fixture with stringLines weakens the changed-text safety tests; the new fixture reads every row afresh and preserves the assertions' distinguishing evidence. Details: js-tests/terminal-files.test.js:287-291 reads rows[abs] per line() call, 671-678 exposes mutable host.lines through a view getter and setLines, and 755-781 mutates a continuation and finally empties the same captured array. Each edit is visible to production FileLinks.download, assets/terminal-files.js:587-595, which rereads view.lines and compares linkRangeText against the hover snapshot before any transfer. stringLines marks rows unwrapped, but terminal-links.js:499-515 snapshots an explicitly supplied range without consulting wrapped; that test invokes hover with link=null to model an OSC label and therefore intentionally does not re-tokenize a printed path. The separate test at terminal-files.test.js:788-819 retains real wrapped/hard-broken cell fixtures, verifies the old rectangle still matches after suffix growth, proves live path recognition differs, and checks refusal and restored admission in both browser/native modes. Contract: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, requires that a partial redraw changing link text withdraw transfer/opening permission; SPEC_impl.md, Session-host file reads, requires printed-path re-recognition and fresh snapshots. Suggested bucket: other (considered test fidelity issue). Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutes the suspected stale fixture or lost wrap coverage as above. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: false for this considered test-fidelity issue; no incorrect shipped transfer route established. Caveat: fixtures model link lines rather than the complete browser renderer; geometry remains integration coverage, as the helper explicitly states.

event.summary: Failed-grid-mount test bypasses the production view getter that throws
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: When a terminal component fails to start, cleanup can replace the useful startup error with an undefined-component TypeError. The rewritten failed-mount test claims to cover that lifecycle but constructs a different view, so it cannot catch the failure. Details: the assigned change rewrites terminal-files.test.js:615-678 to claim the grid's hosting shape and changes 834-848 to test failed construction/disposal. Its view.element getter at 674 returns host.element, which safely returns undefined on failedMount. The shipped grid view in assets/terminal.js:945-950 instead evaluates getGrid().element. createGridSurface at 4302-4313 passes getGrid: () => created before assigning created from farhelmGridTerminal.create; if creation throws, catch at 4356-4358 invokes gridLinks.dispose while created is undefined. FileLinks.dispose at assets/terminal-files.js:641-645 calls clearHover; clearHover at 460-468 evaluates this.view?.element, invoking that getter and throwing before cleanup can rethrow the original err. Optional chaining guards the view object, not an exception inside its accessor. The outer mount catch at terminal.js:4698-4743 ultimately displays Failed to start terminal using this replacement error; no additional resource leak or permanent loss has been established. Contract: the createGridSurface documentation at 4288-4292 explicitly promises failed-build rollback and disposal of links even when the component never exists, and the revised test's 834-836 comment repeats this failed-mount contract.
